hook: Doctor Watson claimed Sherlock Holmes would burn at the stake for his uncanny deductive feats.

sections.voiceover: Doctor Watson claimed Sherlock Holmes would burn at the stake for his uncanny deductive feats.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a 19th-century magnifying glass resting on a handwritten manuscript page.

sections.voiceover: Arthur Conan Doyle published the detective story The Sign of the Four in 1890. Meanwhile, Bram Stoker published Dracula in 1897, featuring a creature of the Carpathian Mountains. How do these powers compare?
sections.visual_cue: A timeline graphic appearing on screen showing 1890 and 1897.

sections.voiceover: Count Dracula inhabits the Carpathian Mountains with physical strength equal to 20 men.
sections.visual_cue: A silhouette icon representing the strength of 20 figures.

sections.voiceover: Count Dracula controls the weather and animal forms but needs formal invitations to enter homes. Arthur Conan Doyle wrote Sherlock Holmes while Bram Stoker created the legendary Count Dracula.
sections.visual_cue: A split screen comparing a Victorian study and a dark, gothic castle landscape.

sections.voiceover: Doyle and Stoker defined the era with their iconic detective and the supernatural vampire.
sections.visual_cue: A final shot of a flickering candle next to a leather-bound book.
